title: introduce-rejoin-latch-anticipatory-shed-and-probe-hysteresis-hotfix
author: Asha Patel
description: Background and motivation: In a recent incident we observed a tight loop of node rejoin attempts combined with aggressive regional probe logic that caused cascading KV-cache evictions and sharp SLO regressions for a small set of tenants. This PR adds three coordinated changes to make graceful degradation more stable: 1) a lightweight rejoin latch that enforces exponential backoff and a short jittered quiet window for nodes that recently left a healthy pool; 2) an anticipatory load-shed controller that uses a moving-window quantile of request latency + KV-pressure to pre-emptively throttle low-priority workloads before hard circuit trips; and 3) probe hysteresis to avoid false-positive regional evictions from spurious probe spikes. The goal is to reduce oscillation during transient congestion while keeping high-priority traffic flowing. Summary of changes: - runtime/scheduler/rejoin_latch.go: new latch with atomic state, per-node cooldown and jittered reopen function. - runtime/shed/anticipatory_shed.go: controller that computes a smoothed 95th latency quantile and a KV-pressure index, emits shed decisions via existing SLO-weighted admission API. - runtime/probe/hysteresis.go: probe smoothing layer with consecutive-success/failure counters and configurable grace window. - telemetry/tags.go: new tags added to request spans (rejoin_latch_state, shed_decision_reason, probe_hysteresis_window) for better post-incident triage. - config/defaults.yaml: conservative defaults for the grace windows and thresholds; documented in comments. - tests/*: unit tests for latch backoff, shed controller heuristics, and probe hysteresis. - docs/runbooks/graceful-degradation.md: runbook section describing operational knobs and how to interpret new telemetry. Implementation notes and tradeoffs: - The rejoin latch uses exponential backoff up to 2m with randomized jitter to prevent thundering; it intentionally favors conservative reopen behavior to avoid rapid reflows. - The anticipatory shed controller is advisory: it marks requests as LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH priority to the admission path instead of outright dropping HIGH priority traffic. This preserves SLA for premium tenants while protecting SLOs for the system. - Probe hysteresis is deliberately small (3 failures / 2 successes default) so it doesn't mask true outages, but reduces noise from flakey dataplane probes. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests added and passing locally - [x] Integration smoke run in staging (latency trace sanity, KV retention) - [x] Telemetry tags verified in staging traces - [x] Config defaults reviewed with SRE - [x] Runbook draft included Risks and mitigation: - Risk: miscalibrated thresholds could cause unnecessary shedding for medium-priority traffic. Mitigation: defaults are conservative; rollout is gated with a gradual config ramp and metric-backed alarms (SLO error budget burn and shed-rate alerts). - Risk: new telemetry increases span cardinality. Mitigation: tags are low-cardinality enums and opt-in via config for high-retention telemetry. Related work: this PR builds on prior adaptive-shed and soft-degradation efforts (see ENG-1987) and should be rolled out in tandem with the kv-preserve sticky lease fixes merged last quarter. Rollout plan: 1) Deploy to a single low-traffic region with shed controller in advisory mode. 2) Monitor shed_rate, 95p latency, and SLO error budget; escalate thresholds if excessive. 3) Enable enforced shedding for non-premium tranches and increase rejoin latch aggressiveness only if probe noise subsides. 4) Full rollout after two days of stable metrics. Links: runbook: docs/runbooks/graceful-degradation.md, incident: https://linear.app/redwood/incident/INC-2025-06-rejoin-thundering
commits: feat(rejoin): add node rejoin latch with exponential backoff
feat(shed): anticipatory shed controller using smoothed latency quantiles
fix(probe): add hysteresis to region probe evaluator
chore(telemetry): attach low-cardinality tags for shed/rejoin decisions
test: unit tests for latch and shed heuristics
small_diffs: rejoin_latch.go: Add RejoinLatch struct (~120 LOC) and tests that simulate repeated disconnects
anticipatory_shed.go: New controller computes EWMA of latency quantiles and emits admission hints
hysteresis.go: Simple counter-based smoothing to require N consecutive fails before marking node unhealthy
review_conversation: Marco Chen (reviewer): Please add a comment clarifying when we escalate a shed from advisory to enforced. Asha: added rollout plan and conservative default values in config/defaults.yaml.

Lena Ortiz (reviewer): Tests look good; can we add a short integration scenario that runs a KV-pressured synthetic to ensure no regressions? Asha: added staging smoke run notes and test harness used for the integration smoke run.
Diego Morales (approver): Verified telemetry tags in staging traces and load test results showing reduced oscillation. Approve to merge once CI passes.
merge_outcome: Merged by squash on 2025-06-14. Commit message condensed to: 'rejoin latch + anticipatory shed + probe hysteresis: reduce rejoin oscillation and protect SLOs'
release_notes: Hotfix: Reduce rejoin oscillation and add anticipatory load-shedding to protect SLOs. Added probe hysteresis to avoid false region evictions. Defaults are conservative; rollout is staged.
post_merge_actions: Monitor shed_rate and 95p latency in rollout region for 48h
If shed_rate > 0.5% for non-premium: reduce shed aggressiveness by 20%
Add dashboard panel for 'rejoin_latch_state' tag distribution
notes: This PR intentionally keeps shed decisions advisory initially to allow live tuning without customer impact. Telemetry tags are low-cardinality to limit cardinality explosion. Contact SRE on-call for immediate rollback.
